profile.summary: MS-BART generates molecular structures from tandem mass spectra by treating the task as translation between token sequences. A MIST encoder first turns the spectrum into a predicted molecular fingerprint; MS-BART reads the fingerprint bits as tokens and writes the molecule as a SELFIES string, using one vocabulary for both. It is pretrained on 4 million simulated fingerprint-molecule pairs, fine-tuned on experimental spectra and then aligned with chemical feedback.

summary_quotes.text: we propose MS-BART, a unified modeling framework that maps mass spectra and molecular structures into a shared token vocabulary, enabling cross-modal learning through large-scale pretraining on reliably computed fingerprint–molecule datasets.
The pretrained model is subsequently transferred to experimental spectra through finetuning on fingerprint predictions generated with MIST
We pretrain MS-BART on a simulated dataset of 4 million fingerprint–molecule pairs.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The backbone is BART-base trained from scratch. Inputs are fingerprints predicted by MIST and binarised with a threshold (0.2 for NPLIB1, 0.11 for MassSpecGym); outputs are canonical SELFIES from a 185-token vocabulary. Pretraining combines three span-denoising tasks and one fingerprint-to-molecule translation task on 4M simulated pairs built from MassSpecGym's unlabelled molecules, excluding molecules close to the test fold. The model is then fine-tuned on MIST fingerprints of experimental spectra, and finally aligned with a chemical feedback step that favours molecules closer to the reference.

quotes.text: We adopt BART-BASE [28] as the backbone of MS-BART, initializing all parameters from scratch
we apply a threshold of ϵ = 0.2 for NPLIB1 and ϵ = 0.11 for MassSpecGym.
Following [15], we employ a vocabulary of 185 SELFIES tokens.
we design three self-supervised denoising tasks for pretraining to recover masked spans, along with one crossmodal translation task to strengthen modality alignment.
The refinement process involved excluding any molecule with an MCES distance of less than two from any molecule in the MassSpecGym test fold.
We therefore introduce a chemical feedback mechanism that guides the model toward generating molecules closer to the reference structure.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The original release on Figshare (article 30393544, CC BY 4.0, published 2025-10-19) holds, for CANOPUS and MassSpecGym, the final model weights, pretrained models, MIST checkpoints and preprocessed data. The current README also supports alternative MIST encoders from FRIGID for the fingerprint step, and notes known path and variable errors in its evaluation scripts. A result should state the MIST encoder, the fingerprint threshold and which stage (pretrained, fine-tuned or aligned) was evaluated.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Sequence-to-sequence language model for de novo structure elucidation from MS/MS via predicted fingerprints.

quotes.text: a unified modeling framework that maps mass spectra and molecular structures into a shared token vocabulary

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: BART-base encoder-decoder trained from scratch, with a MIST spectrum-to-fingerprint encoder in front.

quotes.text: We adopt BART-BASE [28] as the backbone of MS-BART

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Binarised MIST fingerprint predictions for an MS/MS spectrum, as tokens.

quotes.text: To convert MIST probabilities into binary fingerprints, we apply a threshold

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Canonical SELFIES strings for candidate molecules.

quotes.text: To ensure consistency and uniqueness, we use the canonical form of each SELFIES string.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated as a count in the sources read; the model.safetensors files on Figshare are 416,468,904 bytes, which is a file size, not a parameter count.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Pretraining: 4M simulated fingerprint-molecule pairs from MassSpecGym's unlabelled molecules (MCES distance at least 2 from the test fold; also filtered against the NPLIB1 test set for NPLIB1 models). Fine-tuning: MassSpecGym or NPLIB1 (CANOPUS) spectra via MIST fingerprints.

quotes.text: This dataset was generated from a refined subset of the 4M unlabeled molecules provided by MassSpecGym [7].
To prevent data leakage, we further filtered the pretraining set to remove any molecules that were structurally similar or identical to those in the NPLIB1 test set.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Per dataset (CANOPUS, MassSpecGym): a pretrained model and a final model, with their MIST checkpoints, on Figshare article 30393544 version 1.

limitations.text: Depends on MIST fingerprints; errors in the encoder pass straight to the generator, and MassSpecGym in the Wild found problems with some reused MIST checkpoints.

run_guide.summary: Set up the MS-BART environment with uv, download the original weights and preprocessed data from Figshare into data/, and run the MassSpecGym evaluation script after fixing its paths as the README advises.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU (the README's preprocessing examples use cuda:0).
The Figshare archive, downloaded by hand and placed in data/.
